# Nested hydration mismatch sets the component's `vnode.el` to the nested node; the next `<Suspense>` branch is inserted after its siblings (since 3.5.13) (issue #16000)

### Vue version

3.5.44 (also 3.5.13 and 3.5.43; 3.5.12 behaves as expected)

### Link to minimal reproduction

https://play.vuejs.org/#__SSR__

### Steps to reproduce

The reproduction runs in SSR mode, so the preview is rendered with `renderToString` and then hydrated.

`App.vue` renders a container with a `<Suspense>` wrapping `<component :is="page" />`, followed by a `<footer>`. `PageA.vue` has a `<button v-if="show">` nested inside its root `<main>`. `show` is set to `false` in `onServerPrefetch`, so the server renders `<!---->` there and the client renders the button. Hydration logs a node mismatch for that button.

1. Open the reproduction. The output line shows `page A -> footer`.
2. Click "Switch page".

### What is expected?

`page B -> footer`. The new page should take the old page's place, in front of the footer.

### What is actually happening?

`footer -> page B`. The new branch is appended at the end of the container, after the footer. Every later switch also inserts after the footer, until the app is mounted again.

Marking the button's parent with `data-allow-mismatch` silences the warning but not the bug. The console stays empty, and the page still lands after the footer (3.5.44; 3.5.12 keeps the order):

https://play.vuejs.org/#__SSR__

A variant without `<Suspense>` (same pages, `<component :is="page" />` directly before the footer) fails harder. The switch throws `NotFoundError: Failed to execute 'insertBefore' on 'Node': The node before which the new node is to be inserted is not a child of this node.`, followed by `TypeError: Cannot set properties of null (setting '__vnode')`; that is Chromium's wording, and Firefox and WebKit throw their own NotFoundError. The page disappears and only the footer is left. The output line still shows the old order, because the patch throws before it is updated:

https://play.vuejs.org/#__SSR__

With the playground version set to 3.5.12, both reproductions behave as expected.

### System Info

```shell
SFC Playground, SSR mode, Vue 3.5.44: reproduced in Chromium 156, Firefox 157 and WebKit 27.2 (driven by Playwright 1.64).
Version check in Chromium: 3.5.12 OK; 3.5.13, 3.5.43 and 3.5.44 affected.
Originally hit in a Nuxt 4.6.1 app on Vue 3.5.43.
```

### Any additional comments?

**Cause**

`handleMismatch` points the parent component's `vnode.el` at the freshly mounted node, even when that node isn't the component's root:

[link removed]

```ts
// the component vnode's el should be updated when a mismatch occurs.
if (parentComponent) {
  parentComponent.vnode.el = vnode.el
  updateHOCHostEl(parentComponent, vnode.el)
}
```

In the reproduction, `vnode` is the `<button>` inside `PageA`'s `<main>`, so `PageA`'s `vnode.el` becomes the button. Then:

1. When the boundary resolves at the end of hydration, `setActiveBranch` makes `PageA`'s vnode the active branch and copies its `el` (the button) to the Suspense vnode, so `activeBranch.el` is the button.
2. `hydrateSuspense` creates the boundary with a `null` anchor ([Suspense.ts#L858-L871]([link removed])).
3. On the next branch switch, `resolve()` only recomputes the anchor when `parentNode(activeBranch.el) === container` ([Suspense.ts#L608-L620]([link removed])). The button's parent is the `<p>`, so the anchor stays `null`, and `move(pendingBranch, container, null)` appends the new branch after the footer.

Without Suspense, `patchBlockChildren` takes the container for a component vnode from `hostParentNode(oldVNode.el)` ([renderer.ts#L1008-L1024]([link removed])). That is the `<p>`, while the anchor comes from the page's real subtree and is the footer, hence the `insertBefore` error.

These lines came from #12255 (fix for #12253) and first shipped in 3.5.13. They are unchanged on `main` ([0ff253b]([link removed])) and on `minor` / v3.6.0-rc.13, where the condition is `parentComponent && parentComponent.vnode` ([0f59df2]([link removed])).

**Possible fix**

Only update the component's `el` when the mismatched vnode is the component's root, the same guard `setActiveBranch` already uses ([Suspense.ts#L964-L970]([link removed])):

```ts
if (parentComponent && parentComponent.subTree === vnode) {
  parentComponent.vnode.el = vnode.el
  updateHOCHostEl(parentComponent, vnode.el)
}
```

Removing the block instead would bring #12253 back. In that case the mismatched node *is* the component's root (`<CompTrue>` renders a `<div>` where the server left `<!---->`), so the component's `el` has to follow the new node. The guard keeps that case working, because `instance.subTree` is assigned before `hydrateNode` runs on it ([renderer.ts#L1385-L1392]([link removed])). `replaceNode` in the same file already follows this rule: it only rewrites `parent.vnode.el` when that is the node being replaced.

I checked this outside the playground. I patched `vue.esm-browser.js` from the published 3.5.44 and 3.6.0-rc.13 packages. Then I hydrated server HTML (rendered with `@vue/server-renderer` 3.5.43) in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit:

- **With the guard:** the Suspense case keeps `page B -> footer`, and the #12253 toggle still works. The case without Suspense no longer throws (3.5.44 and 3.6.0-rc.13, in all three browsers).
- **With the block removed:** the #12253 toggle throws again (`Cannot read properties of null (reading 'insertBefore')` in Chromium).
- **Unpatched 3.6.0-rc.13:** shows the same wrong order.

The playground's SSR mode doesn't work with 3.6.0-rc.13: `onServerPrefetch` and `onMounted` warn that there is no active component instance. That is why 3.6 was checked outside the playground. I have not run the repo's own test suite with the change.

**Context**

We ran into this in a Nuxt SSG app. A page read browser-only state during setup, which caused a nested hydration mismatch. After landing on that page, every client-side navigation rendered the new page below the app's footer, until a full reload. The footer is rendered after `<NuxtPage>`, and Nuxt renders pages inside `<Suspense>`. The mismatch was our bug and is fixed on our side, but its effect on the page order seemed worth reporting.
